title: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors in Patients With COVID-19: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials Led by the International Society of Hypertension
authors: Gnanenthiran SR, Borghi C, Burger D, Caramelli B, Charchar F, Chirinos JA, et al.; COVID-METARASI Consortium
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
population: 14 randomised trials, 11 contributing data, that assigned adults with COVID-19 to continuation or initiation of an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker against no such therapy; mean age 59 years, 58% men
authorConflicts: Several authors report consultancy fees, speaker honoraria or research support from manufacturers of blood-pressure-lowering drugs, among them Servier, Pfizer, Novartis, Boehringer Ingelheim, Menarini, AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Takeda and Daiichi Sankyo.
result: All-cause mortality within 30 days 7.2% with renin-angiotensin system inhibitors against 7.5% without (relative risk 0.95, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.30), with no difference between ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers. In trials that initiated and continued these drugs, acute kidney injury occurred in 7.0% against 3.6% (1.82, 1.05 to 3.16) and myocardial infarction in 2.1% against 3.6% (0.59, 0.33 to 1.06); dialysis, heart failure, stroke, intensive care admission and ventilation did not differ.
